reconstruction.text: For every pair of Borel probability measures μ and ν on ℝ satisfying ∫ℝ |x|² dμ(x) < ∞ and ∫ℝ |y|² dν(y) < ∞, and every 1-Lipschitz function f: ℝ → ℝ, let Π(μ,ν) be the set of couplings of μ and ν and set W₁ = inf_{γ∈Π(μ,ν)} ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} |x−y| dγ(x,y). Then, in the extended nonnegative reals, max{0, ∫ℝ f(x) dμ(x) − ∫ℝ f(y) dν(y)} ≤ W₁ and W₁ ≤ (inf_{γ∈Π(μ,ν)} ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} |x−y|² dγ(x,y))^{1/2}.

decoder_context: IsProbabilityMeasure asserts that the underlying measure has total mass one. MemLp id 2 is finite second moment for a real measure.
Transport.transportCost c μ ν is the infimum of the nonnegative integral of c over joint measures with marginal laws μ and ν.
WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν is the square root of that infimum for squared norm displacement.
ENNReal.ofReal clips a negative real number to zero and embeds nonnegative real numbers unchanged.

Independently checked both proof halves: integrable pullbacks through the two projections give integral_sub, the norm-integral bound and pointwise Lipschitz estimate bound each feasible linear cost, and two-two Hölder with the constant 1 on a probability plan contradicts any strict separation W₂<W₁ using a feasible root cost below W₁. No minimizer, new hypothesis, or reverse inequality is used. The candidate lesson tracks these steps and correctly distinguishes generic proof from test; its broad phrase about finite mass and normalization should be read with the probability hypothesis and Step 3's explicit unit mass, since finite mass alone does not remove the Hölder factor. assumptions.original: Probability laws, second moments on the common W₂ domain, and a real 1-Lipschitz observable. The hint implicitly uses integrability of the observable.

assumptions.evidence: The proof centers f at 0, obtains L² for the centered function by Lipschitz composition, uses finite mass to pass from L² to L¹, and integrates the constant f(0). Continuity supplies measurability. Neither boundedness nor f(0)=0 is a premise. Unit mass of a coupling follows from its first marginal and supplies the coefficient 1 in Hölder.

conclusion.original: The signed gap Eμ[f]−Eν[f] is at most W₁(μ,ν), which is at most W₂(μ,ν).
conclusion.reconstructed: The nonnegative embedding ENNReal.ofReal of the same signed gap is at most the linear-cost infimum, which is at most the quadratic Wasserstein value.
conclusion.evidence: For a real gap d and a nonnegative W₁, d≤W₁ iff max(d,0)≤W₁. The costs are finite on P₂, e.g. the product plan has finite quadratic cost by |x−y|²≤2|x|²+2|y|², and finite linear cost by Cauchy–Schwarz. The gap has not been reversed or replaced by an absolute gap; there is no equality, duality, or reverse comparison claim.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.CouplingQuadraticIntegrability
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinSpace
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.MeanInequalities

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinLipschitzLower

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

/-- The real P₂ lower comparison in Statistical Optimal Transport §1.8,
Exercise 6. The linear-cost infimum is the literal Kantorovich cost for
absolute displacement; only the one-sided Lipschitz inequality is claimed. -/
theorem expectation_sub_le_linearCost_and_le_wassersteinDistance
    (μ ν : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (hμ : MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 μ) (hν : MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 ν)
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : LipschitzWith 1 f) :
    let W₁ := Transport.transportCost (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal |z.1 - z.2|) μ ν
    ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x, f x ∂μ) - ∫ y, f y ∂ν) ≤ W₁ ∧
      W₁ ≤ WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν := by
  let c : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ := fun z => ENNReal.ofReal |z.1 - z.2|
  change ENNReal.ofReal ((∫ x, f x ∂μ) - ∫ y, f y ∂ν) ≤
    Transport.transportCost c μ ν ∧
    Transport.transportCost c μ ν ≤ WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance μ ν
  constructor
  · have hf_int (ρ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
        (hρ : MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 ρ) : Integrable f ρ := by
      let g : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => f x - f 0
      have hg : LipschitzWith 1 g := LipschitzWith.mk_one fun x y => by
        have heq : g x - g y = f x - f y := by dsimp [g]; ring
        simpa only [Real.dist_eq, heq, NNReal.coe_one, one_mul] using hf.dist_le_mul x y
      have hg₂ : MemLp g 2 ρ := hg.comp_memLp (by simp [g]) hρ
      have hadd : g + (fun _ : ℝ => f 0) = f := by
        funext x
        exact sub_add_cancel (f x) (f 0)
      rw [← hadd]
      exact (hg₂.integrable (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ 2)).add (integrable_const (f 0))
    rw [Transport.transportCost_eq_sInf]
    apply le_sInf
    rintro _ ⟨γ, hγ, rfl⟩
    have hp₁ := CouplingQuadraticIntegrability.measurePreserving_fst_of_isCoupling hγ
    have hp₂ := CouplingQuadraticIntegrability.measurePreserving_snd_of_isCoupling hγ
    have h₁ : Integrable (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => f z.1) γ :=
      hp₁.integrable_comp_of_integrable (hf_int μ hμ)
    have h₂ : Integrable (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => f z.2) γ :=
      hp₂.integrable_comp_of_integrable (hf_int ν hν)
    have he₁ : (∫ z : ℝ × ℝ, f z.1 ∂γ) = ∫ x, f x ∂μ := by
      rw [← hp₁.map_eq, integral_map measurable_fst.aemeasurable hf.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable]
    have he₂ : (∫ z : ℝ × ℝ, f z.2 ∂γ) = ∫ y, f y ∂ν := by
      rw [← hp₂.map_eq, integral_map measurable_snd.aemeasurable hf.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable]
    rw [← he₁, ← he₂, ← integral_sub h₁ h₂]
    calc
      _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∫ z : ℝ × ℝ, ‖f z.1 - f z.2‖ ∂γ) := by
        apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        exact (le_abs_self _).trans (by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using
          norm_integral_le_integral_norm (μ := γ) (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => f z.1 - f z.2))
      _ = ∫⁻ z : ℝ × ℝ, ‖f z.1 - f z.2‖ₑ ∂γ :=
        ofReal_integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm (h₁.sub h₂)
      _ ≤ _ := lintegral_mono fun z => by
        rw [Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs]
        apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        simpa only [c, Real.dist_eq, NNReal.coe_one, one_mul] using hf.dist_le_mul z.1 z.2
  · by_contra! h
    obtain ⟨γ, hγ, hlt⟩ :=
      WassersteinSpace.exists_isCoupling_sqrt_lintegral_lt_of_wassersteinDistance_lt μ ν h
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure γ := Transport.isProbabilityMeasure_of_isCoupling_left hγ
    have hc : Measurable c := by dsimp [c]; fun_prop
    have hq (z : ℝ × ℝ) : c z ^ (2 : ℝ) = WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost z := by
      rw [ENNReal.rpow_two]
      change ENNReal.ofReal |z.1 - z.2| ^ 2 = ENNReal.ofReal (‖z.1 - z.2‖ ^ 2)
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, ENNReal.ofReal_pow (abs_nonneg _)]
    have hCS : (∫⁻ z, c z ∂γ) ≤
        (∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost z ∂γ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := by
      simpa only [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.one_apply, mul_one, ENNReal.one_rpow, lintegral_const,
        measure_univ, hq] using
        ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq γ Real.HolderConjugate.two_two
          (f := c) (g := 1) hc.aemeasurable aemeasurable_const
    exact (not_lt_of_ge
      ((Transport.transportCost_le_lintegral_of_isCoupling c μ ν γ hγ).trans hCS)) hlt

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinLipschitzLower

steps.title: Make the expectations meaningful
steps.text: Subtract the value at zero. The Lipschitz condition bounds the centered function by absolute displacement from zero. Each law has finite second moment and unit mass, so the centered function is integrable; adding back the finite constant preserves integrability.
steps.lean: The Mathlib Lipschitz composition lemma gives MemLp of the centered function. MemLp.integrable on a finite measure and integrable_const handle the two summands.

steps.title: Lower-bound every feasible cost
steps.text: For an arbitrary coupling, project onto its two marginals to rewrite the difference of expectations as one joint integral. Each pullback is integrable. Bound the integrand by its absolute value and then by the cost. Take the infimum after establishing this for every plan.
steps.lean: The two Samplinglib measure-preserving projection lemmas supply the change of measure. Lean compares the nonnegative part of the real difference to the extended nonnegative cost, which is equivalent to the desired real one-sided bound.

steps.title: Compare first and second moments under the same plan
steps.text: Each coupling has unit mass by its first marginal. Use Cauchy–Schwarz with the constant one, then take the quadratic infimum. If W₁ were larger than W₂, a plan whose root cost lies strictly below W₁ would contradict the preceding bound. This is valid without existence of a minimizer.
steps.lean: The Samplinglib strict infimum selection lemma supplies the plan in the contradiction. Mathlib's nonnegative Hölder inequality with p=q=2 compares its two actual costs.

steps.title: Apply the lower comparison to the exercise
steps.text: The two mixture means are zero and m/2. Evaluate with the test f(x)=−x to obtain a positive difference m/2. Combine with the separate common-noise coupling of cost m². Only this last specialization uses the concrete Gaussian means.

lesson.lean_statement: Compare the clipped expectation gap and the literal ENNReal Kantorovich cost to Samplinglib’s quadratic Wasserstein distance.
lesson.lean_proof: Center the Lipschitz observable to justify the two marginal expectations. Pull them back to each coupling, then take the linear infimum. To compare the costs use Hölder on a probability coupling arbitrarily close to the quadratic infimum.
